title: They make the session at God's right hand, and "I am with you," a local presence of the body
pass_a_gloss: Again, that the session at the right hand is to be referred to situation, to ubiety, and is enunciated of the flesh in the abstract; or that this flesh sits at the right hand of God everywhere, not in the heaven into which he ascended — on which inference see us in the Vindication of Mark 16:19. Likewise they: that Christ is said to be with us (Matthew 18:20; 28:20) by a local presence of the body; and that "I am with you" is the same as "my flesh is with you without interval (ἀδιαστάτως)," against Matthew 26:11 and John 17:11. Whereas we hold that it ought more truly to be conceived that Christ is and will always be with his own — namely his Church — by the presence of the divinity, which is common, and likewise by another, special providence of power, grace, assistance, ἐνέργεια, through the influx of the Spirit, and so on. On which matter at length in the Biblical Vindications, Book III, on the place Matthew 18:20.
pass_b_english: Again: that the sitting at the right hand is about place and ubiety, and is said of the flesh in the abstract; or that this flesh sits at God's right hand everywhere, not in the heaven he entered — on that inference see our Vindication of Mark 16:19.

Likewise they take "Christ is with us" (Matthew 18:20; 28:20) as a local presence of the body, and make "I am with you" mean "my flesh is with you without interval (ἀδιαστάτως)," against Matthew 26:11 and John 17:11.

We hold the truer reading: Christ is, and always will be, with his own — that is, with his Church — by the presence of the divinity, which is common to all, and likewise by another, special providence of power, grace, assistance, and ἐνέργεια through the Spirit's influx, and the like.
We have treated that at length in the Biblical Vindications, Book III, on Matthew 18:20.
source_text: Rursus, Sessionem a dextris referendam ad situm, ad ubietatem, & de Carne in abstracto enunciatam esse; aut hanc sedere a dextris Dei ubique, non in Caelo in quod ascendit, qua de illatione nos in Vindic. Marci XVI. 19. Pariter illi, Christum dici, esse nobiscum, Matth. XVIII. 20. XXVIII. 20. praesentia corporis, Locali; & illud, Ego sum vobiscum, idem esse, ac Caro mea est vobiscum ἀδιαστάτως, contra illud Matth. XXVI. 11. Joh. XVII. 11. Dum nos, verius concipi debere Christum nobiscum esse, & fore semper cum suis, nempe Ecclesia sua, praesentia ut Divinitatis, quae communis est, sic speciali altera providentia, virtutis, gratiae, assistentiae, ἐνεργείας, per influxum Spiritus, &c. Qua de re prolixe in Vindic. Biblicis Libr. III. ad Locum Matth. XVIII. 20.
